title: Roving Mixed Migration Project Manager
description:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a qualified Roving Mixed Migration Project Manager  for our operations in Addis Ababa, Dire Dawa and Jigjiga, Ethiopia.

Instruction for applicants:
All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV in English. Please ensure that your CV does not exceed three pages. Applications with CVs longer than the specified limit may not be considered.

Overall purpose of the role: 

Under the supervision of the HOP, the Roving Mixed Migration Project Manager is responsible for the overall management, implementation, quality assurance, and strategic development of mixed migration projects across multiple operational areas in Ethiopia. The role provides leadership in ensuring project activities are implemented in line with DRC’s Mixed Migration Policy and Guidelines, donor requirements, and national frameworks, while responding to the evolving needs of refugees, asylum seekers, returnees, IDPs, and other people on the move.

The role provides leadership in ensuring project activities are implemented in line with DRC's Mixed Migration Policy and Guidelines, donor requirements, humanitarian principles, and national frameworks, while responding to the evolving needs of refugees, asylum seekers, returnees, IDPs, and other people on the move.

The Project Manager will oversee project delivery across different regions, ensure coordination among sectoral teams and partners, support route-based programming, and contribute to evidence-based programme adaptation and advocacy. The role requires frequent travel to operational areas and close engagement with internal and external stakeholders to ensure high-quality, accountable, and context-appropriate interventions.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

Project Management and Programme Quality


	Lead the planning, implementation, monitoring, and closure of mixed migration projects across multiple operational areas.
	Ensure projects are delivered on time, within scope, budget, and quality standards.
	Develop and monitor work plans, procurement plans, and implementation schedules.
	Ensure activities are responsive to context, evidence, and emerging mixed migration trends.
	Conduct regular field monitoring visits to support programme quality and accountability.
	Document lessons learned, best practices, and recommendations to inform programme adaptation.


Budget Management and Financial Oversight


	Serve as Budget Holder for assigned projects.
	Monitor budget utilization, spending forecasts, and financial performance.
	Ensure project expenditures comply with donor regulations and DRC financial procedures.
	Review Budget Follow-Up reports and implement corrective actions when required.
	Support budget development, revisions, and donor budget proposals.
	Identify and mitigate financial risks and support audits and compliance reviews.


Reporting, Grants Management and Compliance


	Ensure compliance with donor agreements, DRC policies, and applicable legal frameworks.
	Lead the preparation and submission of quality donor reports and internal updates.
	Track project progress against work plans, indicators, and contractual commitments.
	Maintain proper project documentation and grant management systems.
	Support donor visits, audits, evaluations, and compliance reviews


Team Leadership and Capacity Building


	Provide supervision, coaching, and performance management to project staff.
	Strengthen staff capacity through mentoring and technical support.
	Promote collaboration, accountability, and learning within project teams.
	Ensure staff understand and apply safeguarding and humanitarian principle


Coordination and Representation


	Represent DRC in relevant coordination forums, working groups, and stakeholder meetings.
	Maintain effective relationships with government authorities, UN agencies, NGOs, donors, and local partners.
	Support route-based coordination and cross-border collaboration on mixed migration issues.
	Contribute to advocacy and strategic engagement based on programme evidence and learning.


Programme Development and Technical Support


	Support assessments, proposal development, and strategic planning processes.
	Ensure mixed migration considerations are integrated across project activities.
	Contribute to evidence generation, analysis, and learning related to migration trends and protection risks.
	Work closely with technical, MEAL, grants, and support services teams to ensure programme quality and impact.

title: Re advertised Supply Chain Assistant - Logistics
description:
Re advertised Supply Chain Assistant- Logistics

The Danish Refugee Council (DRC), one of the world’s leading NGOs, with a focus on responding to displacement, have been registered in Sudan since 2004, delivering life-saving programming in protection, emergency response, shelter, food security and livelihoods, disaster risk reduction, camp management, and humanitarian mine action. DRC has implemented projects in Central Darfur, South Kordofan, Gedaref, Port Sudan, and White Nile. Sudan hosts one of the largest displaced populations in Africa, with over 3.7 million internally displaced people and over 1.1 million refugees from South Sudan, Ethiopia, Eritrea, Central African Republic, Chad, Yemen and Syria. Against a background of political crisis, Sudan faces economic and social turmoil, with sharp increases in food and energy costs, further exacerbated by disease outbreaks and ongoing conflict.

POSITION PROFILE

The overall purpose of the role:

The Supply Chain Assistant Logistics’ main objective is to provide support in the Supply chain department in efficient and effective Logistics implementation and smooth running of departmental operations of capital office with emphasis

support logistics staff and functions including implementation of DRC Dynamics. The role expected to contribute to strengthen the overall supply chain functions. This position will also ensure implementation of audit recommendation related to logistics.

The post holder will be expected to assist the Supply Chain team leader in fixed asset, and fleet management and ensuring that all logistics operations are managed and maintained in an efficient manner as per DRC’s internal and donor procedure & as per the Operations Handbook..

DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

Key Responsibilities: 

Inventory and Warehouse Management


	Assist SCTL for ensuring compliance and implementation of Operations Handbook on inventory and warehouse management at capital level
	Provide monthly comprehensive country report on warehouse inventory to SCTL (list and stock value in hand).
	Assist SCTL in making sure distribution/ Disposal are done on time and on regular bases to have clean up to date records and stock.
	Ensure implementation of all DRC warehousing procedures throughout all WH premises and activities. including Stock/ Bin cards, temperature control, expiry checks etc.
	Proper record of all inventory items for all offices and GH, GPE records to be updated.


Asset Management


	Assist SCTL and support in compliance and implementation of Operations Handbook on asset management.
	Support country & Field SC team for monthly comprehensive country reports on Inventory/Assets, compile all report and provide to SCM
	Making sure that all assets are tagged for all Energy and ICT equipment including the General program equipment
	Put a systematic system in place for reporting for all the related to GPE and equipment list 


Fleet Management


	Maintain fleet management data base and ensure monthly mileage reports are made and analysed.
	Making Sure all Generators under DRC use are well maintained and services regularly as required.
	Assist SCTL for compliance and implementation of Operations Handbook.
	Coordinate Logistics officer and with program and perform right sizing of fleet exercise.
	Ensure an effective fleet management practice in DRC especially for the service contract vehicles for all country 


DRC Dynamics ERP System


	Ensure proper application of DRC Dynamics supply chain processes (mainly P2P and Asset Management) in the operations.


Apply reports and data analytics from ERP supply chain system to improve supply chain performance

SKILLS AND EXPERIENCES


	Minimum 1 years of experience in humanitarian logistics management within the field of Supply Chain Management, Fleet Management, Asset Management, and Distribution Support
	Excellent computer skills in MS Word & Excel, as well as experience working with an ERP system
	Experience with standard procurement procedures and documentation.


Experience working in an (I)NGO

EDUCATIONAL QUALIFICATIONS: (include certificates, licenses etc.)

Bachelor’s Degree in Logistics and Supply Chain Management, Business administration or related field.

Language:

Fluent in both oral and written English, Arabic is desirable

ALL EMPLOYEES ARE EXPECTED TO DEMONSTRATE DRC FIVE CORE COMPETENCIES 


	Striving for excellence: You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.  
	Collaborating: You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.  
	Taking the lead: You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.  
	Communicating: You listen and speak effectively and honestly.  
	Demonstrating integrity: You act in line with our vision and values.


POSITION DETAILS


	Type of contract: National
	Contract Length: 12 months
	Band: Non-management  
	Salary Range Starting from, USD 1,025.00
	Duty station: Port Sudan- Country Office 
	Start date: As soon as possible

title: MEAL Partnership Specialist
description:
MEAL Partnership Specialist

The Danish Refugee Council (DRC), one of the world’s leading NGOs, with a focus on responding to displacement, have been registered in Sudan since 2004, delivering life-saving programming in protection, emergency response, shelter, food security and livelihoods, disaster risk reduction, camp management, and humanitarian mine action. DRC has implemented projects in Central Darfur, South Kordofan, Gedaref, Port Sudan, and White Nile. Sudan hosts one of the largest displaced populations in Africa, with over 3.7 million internally displaced people and over 1.1 million refugees from South Sudan, Ethiopia, Eritrea, Central African Republic, Chad, Yemen and Syria. Against a background of political crisis, Sudan faces economic and social turmoil, with sharp increases in food and energy costs, further exacerbated by disease outbreaks and ongoing conflict.

POSITION PROFILE

The overall purpose of the role:

The MEAL Partnership Specialist supports the strengthening of Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) systems and practices of DRC’s local partners, including national NGOs, CBOs, and volunteer groups such as Emergency Response Rooms and Mutual Aid Groups. 

Working under the supervision of the MEAL Manager and in close coordination and technical guidance from the Partnership Manager/ Partnership Coordinator, the role provides tailored technical support to partners in developing MEAL frameworks, data collection tools, partners’ IPTTs, FCM and reporting systems while ensuring compliance with DRC MEAL standards and donor requirements.

The position focuses on improving data quality, verification of Means of Verification (MoVs), capturing and sharing lessons learnt, and accuracy of reporting practices, including consolidation of indicators in the indicators in the Indicator Performance Tracking Table (IPTT). It also contributes to strengthening partners’ capacities and promoting the use of the data for accountability, learning and program design and improvement.

DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

Support to Local Partners:


	In collaboration with partners and under the guidance of the MEAL Manager, support the design of a logical framework, indicators and MEAL workplans for partner implemented projects.
	Provide ongoing technical support to partner MEAL focal points in developing and reviewing data collection tools for surveys, assessments, and monitoring activities in line with DRC MEAL standards and donor requirement.
	Work closely with Area Office teams to support partners in developing their workplans aligned with agreed objectives and implementation timelines.
	Ensue partners implement verification exercises in line with DRC MEAL SOPs and guidelines.
	Review Means of Verification (MoVs) submitted by partners to ensure quality, completeness, and compliance with project requirements.
	Conduct regular follow-ups with partner organizations to support accurate and timely reporting of achievements.
	Support the documentation and consolidation of reported indicators in the IPTT and ensure alignment with approved logframes.
	Collaborate with partners during planning and implementation of assessments such as baselines, PDMs, and end-lines.
	Reviews partner reports (narrative and MEAL related sections), provide technical feedback and follow up on identified gaps or inconsistencies.


Capacity Strengthening:


	Conducts MEAL Due Diligence (DD) assessments of partners during the onboarding to identify gaps in systems, tools and capacities.
	Contribute to the  development and lead on the implementation of partners capacity building plan from MEAL perspective through technical support for each partner as per their assigned tier (1,2 or 3) resulted from the MEAL DD.
	Conduct targeted coaching and on-the-job mentoring for partner MEAL staff in data collection, quality assurance, and analysis techniques.
	Assist partners in aligning their monitoring tools and methodologies with DRC MEAL minimum operating procedures (MOPs) and donor expectations.
	Facilitate learning and knowledge sharing across partners to improve MEAL practice and use of data.


Monitoring and Evaluation:


	Participate in joint monitoring visits with programme, operations and partner teams as per the agreed monitoring plan.
	Support partners in digital data collection (e.g., KoboToolbox) and ensure a proper data management practices.
	Ensure harmonization and alignment of Scope of work, IPTTs, MEAL Framework, and data collection processes across different partners and sectors.
	Conduct data quality checks, including validation and triangulation of partner reported data against field observations and other sources.
	Identify data inconsistencies and follow up with partners to ensure corrective action are taken
